clue.text: Talks excitedly? Employs profanity, for a start

indicators.note: the profanity is placed at the start, ahead of the word for employs

parts.note: eff is the mild stand-in for the F-word swear
employs means uses

explanation.surface: Someone describing a person who swears as soon as they open their mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush or pour out words is a figurative sense of the verb, matching excited talk; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: Some wheat added to pork pie recipe in the past

parts.note: an ear is a head of wheat
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pork pie recipe that called for some wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a British meat pie; in Cockney rhyming slang the phrase means a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, before now, the comparative of early.

clue.text: Hum renditions of waltzes in time?

indicators.note: the words dance around, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Humming versions of waltz tunes while keeping the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' looks like musical tempo; it is time in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: In relativity, time is treated as a dimension added to the three of space.

clue.text: Team showing age kept out of game

parts.note: a side is a team
a lined face shows its age with wrinkles

explanation.surface: An ageing team is left out of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A player removed from play and left on the bench or touchline is out of the action.

clue.text: Indian master, drawn to both sexes, owns up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole run before it, the bisexual word and owns, is read bottom to top

parts.note: bi is short for bisexual
owns means has

explanation.surface: An Indian master admits to being bisexual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns both pieces together: BI followed by HAS, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonial-era Indian title of respect for a European man, meaning sir or master.

clue.text: Pretended Cliff Richard's back on ecstasy

indicators.note: on places the back of Richard after the ecstasy letter, set upon it

parts.note: a bluff is a steep cliff or headland
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: the back of a name is its final letter, here the end of Richard

explanation.surface: A tabloid rumour that the singer Cliff Richard was back on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a British pop singer, so the name reads as one person; here the cliff is a landform and Richard only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to feign or deceive by pretending, so the past tense matches pretended.

clue.text: Time to put in dirty look as signal of departure

parts.note: blue means smutty or dirty

indicators.note: the time letter is put into the dirty-look pair

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: Choosing the moment to give someone a filthy look as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue flag with a white square is hoisted to show a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Source of milk shake, not quiet

indicators.note: not means the quiet letters are left out

parts.note: a shudder is a shake
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A milkshake made without any quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk shake' reads as a drink, but the definition stops at 'milk'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mammary gland of a cow, from which milk is drawn.

clue.text: Government department's rule: cars included in lifting of tax

indicators.note: the rule and cars go inside the reversed word plus tax
in a down entry, lifting turns the little word upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: to tax is to strain or try
to reign is to rule
Minis are small British cars

explanation.surface: A department's policy that cars are covered when a tax is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns the little word 'of' itself upside down rather than a synonym of it; 'tax' is the verb, as when something taxes your patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry in charge of a country's dealings with other nations is a government department.

clue.text: Unsteady, like teetotaller drinking more rum, mostly

indicators.note: the teetotaller's word takes in the trimmed word

parts.note: a teetotaller is dry, abstaining from alcohol

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: rum means odd, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: A teetotaller oddly drinking rum and wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it is the old British sense of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and tottery from age, the gait of an old person trembling.

clue.text: Ought queen to enter plump and slumped?

indicators.note: the ought-and-queen pair goes into the word for plump

parts.note: plump means rounded
ought means should
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a queen should be chubby and drooping.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooping posture with the shoulders bent forward is a slumped one.

clue.text: What the military gathers from mujahedin, tellingly

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the two words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Intelligence officers learn something revealing from fighters in Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang shortens intelligence, the information an army collects, to this clipped form.

clue.text: Bet pair's involved with it, if so?

definitions.text: Bet pair's involved with it, if so?

indicators.note: involved suggests letters tangled together, so these get rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager on two things together, with a tentative condition attached.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes something split in two: if a pair is involved, the thing is two-part.
explanation.definitionFit: Having two parts or being shared between two parties, as a pair of bettors would be.

clue.text: Opponent of capitalist worker receives demand to pay extra

indicators.note: the communist and the worker take in the demand between them

parts.note: a red is a communist, the capitalist's opponent
to dun is to demand payment of a debt
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A communist worker gets a bill for extra money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surplus to requirements is superfluous, more than needed.

clue.text: As lad dances unclad, this is picked up

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son

indicators.note: unclad means stripped of its outer layer, losing the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boy strips off for a dance and gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A resemblance of vowel sounds in words is something heard by the listener's ear.

clue.text: Extremes of creamy New York confectionery

parts.note: the extremes, the first and last letters, of creamy are ..., which spoken as a pair run together

explanation.surface: Something very rich and sweet sold in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as 'C and Y', the two outer letters run together into the American word for sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call sweets by this word, so it is the confectionery of a New Yorker.

clue.text: People on stage habitually forgetting line? Their craft deserts them

parts.note: a cast is the actors in a play

indicators.note: forgetting means the line letter is dropped

parts.note: habitually means always

explanation.surface: Actors who keep forgetting their lines find their skill abandoning them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like acting skill; it is a boat that has left them shipwrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipwrecked sailors are left stranded when their vessel is lost.

clue.text: Migrant from Scotland's sane

parts.note: in Scots 'no' means not
sane is 'not mad', which in the Scots form is no mad

explanation.surface: A traveller who comes from Scotland is perfectly sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots speech 'no' means not, so a sane Scot is 'no mad'; read as one word that is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home, moving from place to place, is a migrant.

clue.text: Vengeance of Greeks in mess, introduction of euro having failed

indicators.note: having failed suggests something collapsed into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Greece is in a mess after the euro was brought in and failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of retribution, whose name stands for righteous punishment.

clue.text: Dwelling on outskirts of Stirling hosts very Gallic function

indicators.note: the outer letters of Stirling hold the French word and the function
the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: très is French for very
sin is short for sine, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A home on the edge of Stirling, a Scottish city, hosting a very French party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwelling' looks like a noun for a house; it is a verb, as in dwelling on a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelling on a point means emphasising it repeatedly, laying weight on it.

clue.text: Fool withdraws support round river, up which you're stuck

indicators.note: withdraws means draws back, so the word for fool reads backwards

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool

indicators.note: the support goes round the river letter

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A fool takes away a prop round a river and is left in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up a gum tree' is a British idiom for being in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means in a predicament with no escape.

clue.text: Love to get boost after day lacking variety

indicators.note: the love and boost pair come after the day

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
love is zero in tennis, a circle O
a tonic is a pick-me-up, a boost

explanation.surface: Someone in love gets a lift after a dull day.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging in tone or pitch, so dull and without variation.

clue.text: Capital of Kentucky, boring as well

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the state code goes inside

parts.note: as well means too
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: The capital of Kentucky is dull too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Kentucky' wants to be Frankfort; the definition is only 'Capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese capital city, seat of the government of Japan.

clue.text: Skip training held by coach

indicators.note: the training letters are held inside the coach word

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a car
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Missing training session overseen by the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' looks like missing a session; it means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or frisk about playfully, as in a skip.

clue.text: Gnome repelled me abroad, going after a kiss

indicators.note: the reversed French word follows the a and the kiss

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the French word reads backwards

parts.note: moi is French for me

explanation.surface: A garden gnome rejected an advance overseas after being kissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' looks like a garden ornament; it means a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a maxim or aphorism, a short statement of a general truth.

clue.text: Fancy scarlet? It's donned by leader power dressing

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are worn around the leader and power, which sit inside
fancy as in fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: a king is a leader
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A ruler puts on a striking red outfit as power dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power dressing' reads as a fashion phrase, but the power is just a letter and the dressing is a first-aid bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive bandage put over a cut is a wound dressing.

clue.text: Sailor wearing loose jeans in US city

indicators.note: the sailor is inside the jeans letters, wearing them
loose means shaken free of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in baggy jeans in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges JEANS to SANJE, and the sailor sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large Californian city at the south of San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Snap tersely: "Go for another look"

indicators.note: snap as in break, so the following word is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A curt instruction to change one's image.
explanation.definitionFit: To give hair or clothes a new style is to change appearance, adopting a different image.
